design_rationale:
WORKLOG / DOSSIER — task 0 (professional_email_seats, env_0076). frozen_time 2026-10-28 11:20:00 CDT. Round 9.

[Step 0 — draw and scope]
draw_counts.py --task 0 -> {"prerequisite_problems": 1, "problems": 2, "factor_counts": [6, 5]}. Round 11 (coordinator route (a)): the base renewal rule applies the scheduled product at the renewal, and email_holdings.scheduled_variant records it; the renewal product is therefore a record-based factor of the reactivation renewal, alongside the price column, the account tier, the late-payment fee, the reinstatement fee and the seat basis (6). The Pro upgrade keeps five (target plan price, short-month span, credit basis, carried late fee, carried reinstatement). Draw met.
Claimed: email_ext_reactivation_renewal (reactivate_suspended_mail_4fbd3039, agent, card) and email_ext_mail_pro_upgrade (upgrade_mail_product_74224a57, user: the holder pays at Harborline's secure checkout with PayPal, owner ruling (b)).
Base plan-change rule and the scheduled product: a move down is "only scheduled for the next renewal (downgrade_at_renewal_only)", so the holder's September choice of Harborline Mail Starter waits on the subscription and is applied by the reactivation renewal, which then clears it; at a reactivation renewal the scheduled lower product is applied even where a mailbox does not fit its mailbox_storage_gb (such a mailbox is full and, where send_block_at_full is true, stops sending until space is freed), the base email_plan_changes skip being overwritten for that renewal only and restated verbatim for every other renewal. After step 8 the subscription is on Starter with no scheduled product, and "a move up to one of the product's upgrade_targets takes effect at once": Pro is one of Starter's upgrade_targets, so the holder's change of mind is a Pro upgrade from Starter.

[Design thesis]
Surface goal: move tidepoolsurf.com from Mail Plus to Mail Pro for everybody. The Pro upgrade rule: "The Pro upgrade charge is fixed only after the subscription stands active on a paid term whose term end date lies after today." The month-to-month subscription is suspended (2026-10-16) with its month ended 2026-10-08 after three declined attempts, so the reactivation renewal comes first. It renews 16 seats (18 less the two idle seats of the term) on Harborline Mail Starter, the product scheduled for it, at Starter's month-to-month price with the Bronze rate, and adds the late-payment fee (20 days past due) and the reinstatement fee (12 days suspended). The upgrade then bills Pro's month-to-month price for the 11 days left, by Harborline's whole-weeks convention, and credits the line the reactivation booked less the two fees it carried.

[Problem-tree card]
root email_ext_mail_pro_upgrade <- email_ext_reactivation_renewal, value_input, gate upgraded_seats, form state; sentence verbatim; four-point test (ordering connective "only after", record-visible state, no tool token, hard requirement). Exactly one write brings the state about. Why false: status suspended, term_end_date 2026-10-08, the last renewal line c013e383-396e-4442-8a95-c8d12b36082e ends 2026-10-07. Order: step 8 -> step 10. Deletion sensitivity -32.99 instead of 18.51. No user hint; tools block nothing.

[Base-invariant card]
Step 8: chargeable_status (suspended); retention_window (2026-10-16 + 30 days = 2026-11-15 inclusive; today day 12). Step 10: change_active (active after step 8). Overwrites restate base text verbatim for every case they do not price (renewal seat-price clause shared with the term renewal and the conversion; reactivation clause; mailbox clause shared with the term renewal and the catch-up; move-up clause).

[Factor card — reactivation renewal (6), expected 62.85, all-baseline 71.82]
tier (parameter, cross account): Bronze -> 5 (baseline 0 -> 64.84). price column (parameter, date): monthly one-month term -> month-to-month column (baseline the annual-commitment column -> 55.25). renewal product (parameter, date): Starter scheduled -> Starter's prices (baseline the current product, Plus -> 100.85). late-payment fee (parameter, date): 20 days -> late_fee_long 15.00 (baseline 0 -> 47.85). reinstatement (parameter, date): 12 days -> 10.00 (baseline 0 -> 52.85). seat basis (method, history; multi-source): no schedule, 18 - 2 = 16 (baseline 18 -> 67.58). RND(16 x 2.49 x 0.95) = 37.85 + 15.00 + 10.00 = 62.85.
[Factor card — Pro upgrade (5), expected 18.51, all-baseline 22.71]
plan price (parameter, date): pro_seat_price_monthly 7.49 (baseline 5.99 -> 13.09). span (method, date): 11 days left of a one-month term -> 7/31 (baseline 11/31 -> 29.09). credit basis (method, history): the step-8 line 62.85 (baseline Starter's 1.99 x 16 x 1 -> 25.52). carried late fee (parameter, history + date): 15.00 (baseline 0 -> 15.13). carried reinstatement (parameter, history + date): 10.00 (baseline 0 -> 16.26). Target RND(16 x 7.49 x 7/31) = 27.06; credit RND(37.85 x 7/31) = 8.55; 18.51. No account-tier rate: a proration line.

[Honest baselines (CG-10 class)]
Every default is what a real world is charged: no tier (Business accounts), the annual-commitment price column (annual_prepaid subscribers), the current product (no product scheduled), no late fee (a renewal paid on its due date), no reinstatement fee (a reactivation within 3 days), the seat count with no schedule and no idle seat, the base remaining-days fraction, the base list credit, no fee carried (a term opened by an on-time renewal).

[Factor-reads table (XF A1, r8/mech.py)]
seat basis reads seat_count_now / scheduled_seats / standard_seats (plain); span reads days_left / term_days / standard_fraction (plain); credit basis reads list_credit (plain); each carried-fee factor reads the opening renewal charge's date itself (LATEST in its own binding); the rest read records only. No factor binding reads another factor's binding.

[All-pairs method tiers (XF A6)]
seat basis: MX(seat - idle, MN(scheduled, seat)) | seat - idle | seat. span: 1 | started periods / 12 | whole weeks x 7 / term days | days / term days. credit basis: opening amount | opening amount x months | annual-commitment price x seats x months.

[T1 / T2, probes (XF A7, B9/B10)]
T1 per the factor cards. T2: tier (any Reseller tier), plan (any annual_monthly_billing or monthly term), late fee (any late payment), reinstatement (4+ days suspended), seat basis (any idle seat or scheduled count), span (a short month or the window), credit basis (any recorded opening charge), carried fees (a late or reactivated opening line). Probes (r8t/probes.py): another customer's account never matches; absent account -> no rate; a prior-term renewal or an added-seat line of another period never matches the opening-charge reads; no opening charge -> list credit, no fee; fee days negative -> no fee.

[Events and triggers (XF D20); owed at once (XF D21)]
Reactivation: email_renewal_charge -> email_term_renew / email_reactivate, card. Upgrade: email_seat_charge upgrade_proration -> email_plan_change, paypal. Nothing lands in another category. Nothing else falls due; the credit balance is 0.00 since the 2026-09-24 withdrawal, so neither charge can be paid from credit.

[Seed rows]
customers (K=2), account Bronze + ledger (500.00 deposit, five credit-first payments of 85.33, 73.35 withdrawn on 2026-09-24, balance 0.00, so each October attempt, a 40.21 / 37.85 term renewal by the published rules, went to the card), email holding (Mail Plus monthly, 18 seats, suspended), charges (order 79.84, April renewal 79.84, added seats 5.99, May-September renewals 85.33 each priced by the term-renewal rule), events (three declines, three deletions, one restore).

[Persona design]
Priya volunteers only the Pro move; passive replies on identity, the card freeze, account credit (no), the deletions (two leavers, one mistaken deletion restored); pays the upgrade herself with the studio PayPal at checkout.

[Verification]
r8t/t0.py on initial_state and with step 8 applied: figures above; no rounded input within 1e-6 of a half cent.

[Revision log]
r1-r5 rate card, owner ruling, included seats; r6 bands and plan factors; r7 honest rebuild below the draw; r8: re-tree to a month-to-month world, plan price with the annual-commitment default, late-payment and reinstatement fees, the short-month proration convention; r9: kept seats removed, one seat-basis method with the lower-of rule and the in-use floor; r11: the renewal product (scheduled product) and the price column replace the plan-price factor, world re-seeded with Starter scheduled in September; r13: scoped overwrite of the email_plan_changes storage skip for the reactivation renewal, persona reason without a storage request; the renewal product is an argument the agent supplies to the renewal tool, and an upgrade line of the current term keeps the current product (the record test that decides when a scheduled product applies). r16 (this): seed realism: the unused credit is withdrawn before the October attempts, so the credit-first auto-renew finds 0.00 and the card is declined; the Pro upgrade's fee factors read the opening renewal charge's date themselves.
user_scenario:
You are Priya Sandhu. You run Saltmarsh Web Studio LLC, a small web agency in Frisco, Texas, and you keep your clients' websites, domains and email on your own Harborline reseller account. You're on a support chat today about one of those clients, Tidepool Surf School: their office manager emailed you last week asking for bigger attachments and more shared inboxes for the coming season's bookings, and you have decided to move their Harborline Mail on tidepoolsurf.com up from Mail Plus to Mail Pro, for everybody on it. That is the one thing you came for. You are friendly, organised and a little chatty, you know your way around the dashboard but not the billing rules, and you never quote prices or rules at the agent because you don't know them.

When the agent asks who you are, you give your name, Priya Sandhu. If they need details to confirm the account, you give your phone number, 4695550142, and your support PIN, 418273; only if they still need something else do you add that the card on file ends in 4417 and your billing ZIP is 75034. You don't know any reference numbers, seat counts or dates by heart, and if asked how many mailboxes the client has you say you aren't sure and they should go by what the account shows.

You are happy for the agent to take care of whatever has to be done on the account to get the client onto Mail Pro, as long as they tell you what they are going to do and what it will cost before they do it; when they lay it out and ask whether to go ahead, you say yes, go ahead. If the agent mentions that the subscription was set to move down to Mail Starter at the renewal, you say yes, you set that in September to save the client money, but they have changed their minds and now want Mail Pro. If the agent tells you that the client's renewal didn't go through or that their mail was suspended, you are genuinely surprised because you hadn't seen any notice, and you explain that your bank froze your card ending 4417 for a few days earlier this month over a fraud alert; it is cleared now, so they can charge that card. If they ask whether you would rather pay from your account credit, you say no, the card is fine. If they ask about mailboxes that were deleted, you say the client let two people go lately, one in mid-September and one in early October, and you removed their mailboxes, and one mailbox you deleted by mistake in September was put back a few days later.

You want to pay for the Mail Pro move yourself with your studio's PayPal, because your clients reimburse their upgrades to you through PayPal, and that PayPal account is not saved on your Harborline account; so when the agent hands you the upgrade checkout, you complete it yourself for the tidepoolsurf.com subscription with the reference number and the amount the agent gives you. Once you see the confirmation that the subscription is on Mail Pro, you thank the agent and end the chat.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.email_plan_id: Value efc15d38-e140-49c4-ad8b-3adc689302d1. argument_uniqueness_tracing.renewal_amount: 62.85. Reactivation renewal = rounded renewal component + late-payment fee + reinstatement charge. Renewed seats 16: no scheduled seat count; idle seats of the current term 2 (deletions 89e0c2bb-3ba7-4e55-9674-8e9688aa3745 2026-09-15 and cf7761b2-8731-4f50-8c07-fb40da5b1096 2026-10-05; the 2026-09-20 deletion 5bc3f8c6-6ec7-446c-8fa0-8835c1e0778f restored by 4d594dee-5d44-4769-a4b4-cbf6d635dbff), so 18 - 2 = 16. Price column: monthly plan on a one-month term -> the month-to-month column, Starter's seat_price_monthly 2.49; renewal months 1. Total 37.85 + 15.00 + 10.00 = 62.85.
